verdict.probe_answer: Test files are byte-identical between arms (both transcribed the plan's 7 fixtures verbatim; diff hunk offsets confirm identical +320-line insertions) — test rigor is equal by construction, so the arms cannot be differentiated on test authorship. All 7 would fail on pre-change code: the two-crate collision test would stay 2xNameOnly (no owner-prune existed), the inherent+trait test would DROP (old graph_target_resolution declines on ids==2), the three keep-all tests (block-local glob, macro wildcard, Pending-alias-over-collision) would wrongly prune/drop under a naive exact-ident or global-search oracle, and the free-fn-misroute test would wrongly mint a cross-module method under the pre-guard code — genuine regression detectors, not tautologies. Strongest test (shared): scope_graph_free_fn_path_not_misrouted_to_colliding_method_pool — deliberately cross-module so it discriminates the real fix from a same-scope fixture that wouldn't even compile (E0428), and pins the resolved file/confidence exactly. Weakest test (shared): scope_graph_macro_wildcard_shadow_keeps_all — asserts only 'all remaining are NameOnly' via .all() without asserting resolved.len() (unlike the block-local-glob sibling test), so it would vacuously pass if the pool were empty.
verdict.rationale: Structurally the two diffs are the same patch: identical rust_scope_prune_owner, owner_method_key, integration control-flow, and an identical 320-line test block. The one real divergence is rust_graph_qualified_target_is_free_fn. The task brief itself specifies this guard's exact contract: '... resolves to a non-empty id-set all NOT in method_owners -> accept the shipped graph free-fn resolution, skip the prune.' Arm A implements this literally (`!ids.is_empty() && ids.iter().all(...)`). Arm B uses `!ids.iter().any(|fid| method_owners.contains_key(*fid))`, which is vacuously true for an EMPTY id-set — contradicting the brief's explicit 'non-empty' requirement. Concretely: for a qualified `::` site whose authoritative graph target resolves to an empty id-set (the brief's own example: a trait's signature-only UFCS declaration) colliding by bare name with an unrelated method pool, Arm B's guard fires and short-circuits straight to the shipped resolve-or-drop path without ever considering the owner-prune's disproof machinery, whereas Arm A treats this as NOT a free-fn (matching spec) and instead falls into the owner-prune/fail-open branch, additionally adding an explicit 'definite decline' check so an empty id-set still can't fail-open into `owner_lookup_in_modules`'s stem-guess floor. Arm A both matches the literal plan text and reasons more carefully about the recall-vs-precision invariant the whole task is built around; Arm B silently broadens a spec'd helper's contract. No provided test exercises this exact combination, so it's not a shipped-test failure, but it is a concrete, brief-grounded deviation, not speculative internals — enough to call Arm A materially better on faithfulness to Task 5's specification even though both are otherwise complete, in-scope, and equally tested.
